conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: ALPHABET clause (ordinal number of characters in the native coded character sets)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Row written from CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs: Ord(string) = s[0]+1; Char(long)/CharNational(long) accept 1..65536 (c = n-1, > 0xFFFF refused with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i8.cob --std 2023: ORD("A")=66, ORD(X"FF")=256, ORD(X"00")=1, ORD('€')=8365, ORD(N"A")=66, ORD(N'€')=8365, CHAR(66)=A, CHAR(8365)=€, CHAR-NATIONAL(66)=A. cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 'The implementor shall define the order of characters within the native alphanumeric coded character set' OK (6). Adjacent open defect named in the row, not stated as behaviour: HIGH-VALUE ORD=256 although € is 8365 — kb/Work PB1093 (open). PB1092 (open) lists item 8 as owed; this row discharges that part. No spec-derived pin (—).
rows.rule-text: ALPHABET clause (ordinal number of characters in the native coded character sets). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.3.7, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, General rule 6)

rows.subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.6.4 "If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified, the value of the associated alternate record key shall not be equal" -> OK GR4; cross-checked §14.9.51.4 GR42 c) (WRITE '22', --check OK) and §9.1.13.2 2) c) ('02' for a duplicate on a DUPLICATES key). Probe gr4.cob (2023): unique alt key duplicate WRITE -> INVALID KEY '22'; REWRITE creating a duplicate -> '22'; WITH DUPLICATES key duplicate WRITE -> '02'. The collating-sequence half: file G with `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF G-ALT IS FOLD` (ALPHABET FOLD "A" ALSO "a" "B" ALSO "b") - keys "Ab" and "aB" are equal under that sequence and the second WRITE -> '22', so equality is judged under the file's collating sequence (KeyEq -> KeyCompare with the key's weights). Both halves verified. No existing spec-derived test pins the '22'/'02' on an alternate key (grep of tests/conformance ALTERNATE goldens: none asserts 22 on a unique alternate), so test-ref is empty. NOTE: the duplicate check is also where the GR6 suppression defect surfaces (spurious '22' between two records whose keys equal a figurative/short SUPPRESS WHEN value) - that is GR-12.4.5.6.4-6's mechanism, not this rule's.
rows.rule-text: The DUPLICATES phrase specifies that the value of the associated alternate record key may be equal to the value of the same alternate record key in another record in the physical file. If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified, the value of the associated alternate record key shall not be equal to the value of the same alternate record key in another record in the physical file. The equality or inequality is based on the collating sequence used for the file according to the rules for a relation condition.

rows.subject: ANY LENGTH clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: function - 'shall be referenced in its procedure division header as a formal parameter with the BY REFERENCE phrase' (cite.py --check 13.18.2.3 OK). `UnitIsFunction ? !formal` where formal excludes BY VALUE. Probe p6.cob (FUNCTION-ID): unreferenced M -> 1542 SR4; ANY LENGTH RETURNING R -> 1542 SR4 (correctly illegal for a function, unlike SR3b); BY REFERENCE formal L accepted. Positive leg golden conformance:2002/any_length_function; no golden pins the reject half (RETURNING / unreferenced in a function), so test-ref left empty (test-needed). || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO 2023 Annex E lists no substantive change to 13.18.2, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; the 2002 introduction is the project's COBOL-2002 gate and is not derivable from the 2023 text alone - see dossier gap)
rows.rule-text: If the source element containing the ANY LENGTH clause is a function, the subject of the entry shall be referenced in its procedure division header as a formal parameter with the BY REFERENCE phrase.

rows.subject: ARITHMETIC clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: `ARITHMETIC IS {NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL}`, ARITHMETIC and the three phrases underlined, IS not underlined, plain braces = exactly one (cite.py --check 11.9.5.1 "STANDARD-DECIMAL" -> OK §11.9.5.1 General format; cite.py --check E.2 "Standard Arithmetic" -> OK §E.2 21)). Code: arithmeticClause = ARITHMETIC IS? arithmeticMethod; arithmeticMethod = NATIVE | STANDARD_BINARY | STANDARD_DECIMAL | STANDARD. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/arithmetic-clause/p_*.cob) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: every alternative with and without IS compiles at 2014/2023 and selects the right engine (FUNCTION SQRT(2) into PIC 9V9(30): NATIVE/absent -> binary64 1.414213562373095145474621858738, STANDARD-DECIMAL -> 34-digit 1.414213562373095048801688724209); `ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE STANDARD-DECIMAL` -> COBOL0307 (exactly one); `ARITHMETIC IS.` -> COBOL0001 (one required); STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2002 -> COBOLNET0900; OPTIONS at 85 -> COBOLNET0804; the 2002 STANDARD phrase compiles at 2002, warns obsolete (0903) at 2014, is rejected at 2023 (0807, Annex E.2 item 21 removal) - edition-correct dual window. STANDARD-BINARY is refused by COBOLNET0806 at every edition: a documented processor-dependent decline (A.3 item 2, cite --check A.3 OK; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2, kb/Work PB198), not a syntax defect; at 2023 it additionally draws the NOTE 2 obsolete warning 0903 (cite --check 11.9.5.2 "The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature" OK). Grammar comment calls bare STANDARD 'a common vendor spelling' - it is in fact the ISO 2002 phrase; the gating is right, the comment is stale. No single existing test exercises the IS-omitted spelling plus each alternative, so test-ref is empty (candidates: conformance:2023/l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate writes ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE; conformance:2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal writes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002 (clause introduced with the OPTIONS paragraph; NATIVE | STANDARD); 2014 (STANDARD-BINARY, STANDARD-DECIMAL added; STANDARD obsolete); 2023 (NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL; Standard Arithmetic removed - Annex E.2 item 21); not in 1985
rows.rule-text:
╭ NATIVE ╮ │ │ ARITHMETIC IS ┤ STANDARD-BINARY ├ │ │ ╰ STANDARD-DECIMAL ╯
> **Figure notes (ARITHMETIC clause syntax diagram).** `ARITHMETIC`, `NATIVE`, `STANDARD-BINARY`, and `STANDARD-DECIMAL` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` is **not** underlined. The braces are plain — exactly one of the three alternatives shall be selected.

rows.subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The result of implied insertion shall comply with the rules of Table 5, Combinations of conditions, logical operators, and parentheses." cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.3 -> OK. The inserted relation is bound through the SAME CheckedRelational construction as a written relation and nested in the ordinary logical tiers, so Table 5 adjacency is enforced by the condition grammar: probes `A = B AND NOT NOT C` and `A = B AND NOT NOT < C` -> COBOL0001 (NOT NOT not admitted); `A = B OR NOT` -> COBOL0001; a parenthesized sub-condition starts a fresh scope (BindPrimary) so no insertion crosses a parenthesis. No spec-derived test targets the rejection side (test-needed).
rows.rule-text: The result of implied insertion shall comply with the rules of Table 5, Combinations of conditions, logical operators, and parentheses.

rows.subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If the data description of the receiving data item does not include an explicit decimal point specification, the data item is treated as if it had an assumed decimal point immediately following its rightmost digit.' cite.py --check 14.6.8.2 -> OK §14.6.8.2 3). Code: a PICTURE with no V/'.' and no P gets scale afterV=0 (point after the rightmost digit); P-scaled pictures get the point after the P run (trailing) or before it (leading), which is the PICTURE's own decimal-point specification. Probe out/probe/alignment/p1.cob and p2.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 85 and 2023 identical): MOVE 123.456 TO PIC 9(5) -> 00123; MOVE 7.9 TO PIC ZZ9 -> '  7'; MOVE 0.5 TO PIC 99 -> 00; MOVE PIC 9(3)V9(3) 987.654 TO PIC 9(5) -> 00987; P scaling MOVE 12345 TO 99PPP -> 12000, MOVE 0.00789 TO PP9 -> 0.00700; DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA receiver PIC ZZ.ZZ9 (period = insertion, no decimal point) MOVE 12345,6 -> '12.345', PIC ZZ9PP MOVE 12345 -> '123'. All match the rule. No golden cites rule 3 discriminatingly (l1_subtract_giving_resultant_categories stores the integer 19, which cannot distinguish the assumed point) -> test-needed. [code-location note: (scale = trailingP>0 ? -trailingP : leadingP>0 ? leadingP+digitPositions+floatingExtra : afterV, line 354); code-location note: arm (NumericRenderer.StoreExpr at target.OperandPic.Scale)] || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (common §14.6.8.2 rule, no edition qualification in the clause)
rows.rule-text: If the data description of the receiving data item does not include an explicit decimal point specification, the data item is treated as if it had an assumed decimal point immediately following its rightmost digit.

rows.subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If the receiving operand is a fixed-point numeric-edited item, further alignment, zero fill or truncation, and transfer of digits take place as described in the general rules and editing rules in 13.18.40, PICTURE clause.' cite.py --check 14.6.8.2 -> OK §14.6.8.2 5). The rule is a delegation: the MOVE aligns at the mask's scale and hands the digits to CobolEdit.Format, the §13.18.40 editor. Probe out/probe/alignment/p1.cob (85 and 2023 identical) and p2.cob, each expected image derived from §13.18.40.5/.6: Z,ZZ9.99 <- 1234.567 = '1,234.56' (fraction truncation right); ---9.9 <- -12.5 = ' -12.5'; ZZZ.ZZ <- 0 = all spaces; ***9.99 <- 5.1 = '***5.10'; $$$,$$9.99 <- 12345.678 = '$12,345.67'; 999CR <- -5/+5 = '005CR'/'005  '; 99B99/99 <- 12345 = '01 23/45'; 999.99 <- 12345.678 = '345.67' (high-order truncation); +++9 <- 5 / -1234 = '  +5' / '-234'; 999DB <- -7 = '007DB'; ZZ9.99 BLANK WHEN ZERO <- 0 = spaces; 000999 <- 42 = '000042'; comma mode ZZ9,99 <- 12,345 = ' 12,34'; $$$9 <- 12345 = '$345'. All observed as derived. Individual §13.18.40 editing rules are owned by their own rows; this row's delegation (alignment at the mask's decimal point + truncation/zero fill + transfer to the editor) is verified. Covering spec-derived golden conformance:2023/l1_picture_special_insertion cites §14.6.8.2 rule 5 and derives [0003.50] from the rule text. || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty: l1_picture_special_insertion does not pin the truncation half of rule 5) — On behavior the verdict holds. 27 additional §13.18.40 edge images all matched, including floating and zero-suppression rule b) at zero and non-zero, '*' replacement keeping the point (commas become '*'), B/0// inside floating strings, a multi-character CURRENCY string, CR/DB/trailing '-', de-editing a numeric-edited sender, and an alphanumeric sender. The cited golden is the problem. It is a §13.18.40.5 rule-4 (special insertion) fixture: it pins alignment and zero fill (3.5 into 9(4).99 and 9.9(4)) but never truncation at either end. Rule 5 names 'alignment, zero fill or truncation, and transfer of digits', so a test covering one half of the rule cannot close the row. The row should stay CONFORMS-untested until a golden truncates at both ends, for example 999.99 <- 12345.678 -> '345.67' and ZZ9.9 <- 1.99 -> '  1.9'. [code-location note: arms (NumericRenderer.StoreExpr at the mask scale — MoveEmitter.SenderContext / RuntimeApi.ReceiverScaleOf)] || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (common §14.6.8.2 rule; the §13.18.40 editing symbols it delegates to carry their own edition rules)
rows.rule-text: If the receiving operand is a fixed-point numeric-edited item, further alignment, zero fill or truncation, and transfer of digits take place as described in the general rules and editing rules in 13.18.40, PICTURE clause.

rows.subject: Alignment of alphanumeric group items (relative to first elementary item)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Row written from the code: RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth sums subordinate widths with no padding term and OffsetOf advances by the same widths, so every group (alphanumeric or strongly-typed) is coincident with its first item. Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i6.cob (--std 2023): 01 G (9(4) COMP, X) BYTE-LENGTH 3 and CONVERT(G ANY ANUM HEX)=01025A (G1=258 occupies bytes 1-2), strongly-typed SG (9(4) COMP-5, X) 3, K (N, X) 3. Refuter probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/refute-probe/r6.cob: a bit item followed by PIC X is 2 bytes (the §8.5.1.6.3 filler bits), so the row's 'sum of sizes / none between items' claim is qualified for bit items; strongly-typed POINTER-first group 9, SYNC items unpadded (S=14). cite.py --check 8.5.1.6.1 and 8.5.1.6.5 OK. No spec-derived golden pins the group-start offset directly (test-ref empty; row says —). 8.5.1.6.5 applies from 2002; 8.5.1.6.1 at every edition. Owning note: A11 umbrella / PB1522 step 3.
rows.rule-text: Alignment of alphanumeric group items (relative to first elementary item). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.5.1.6.1, Alignment of alphanumeric groups and of data items of usage display and 8.5.1.6.5, Alignment of strongly-typed group items)

rows.subject: Alphanumeric literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "Character-1 may be any character in the coded character set" OK. STR_BODY admits every code point except the delimiter (undoubled) and CR/LF (which end the line, so cannot be literal content in any reference format); the compile-time alphanumeric set is UTF-16 (project charset decision), so nothing the source set can carry is refused. Probe p11: e-acute and a CJK ideograph in a Format 1 literal compile and round-trip. NOTE 1's UTF-8/mixed option is permissive ('neither required ... nor prohibited') and not provided. No spec-derived golden pins non-ASCII Format 1 content -> test-ref empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held)
rows.rule-text: Character-1 may be any character in the coded character set that the implementor has chosen for source code representation and designated as a character in the compile-time alphanumeric coded character set. NOTE 1 This allows, but does not require, characters in an alphanumeric literal to be represented in source code in a national coded character set. This permits, for example, a literal of the form "ABC" to be represented in the source code in UTF-16 and stored as ISO/IEC 646. This is essential in order to allow source code to be represented entirely in a coded character set such as UTF-16, but is not restricted to that case. An implementation is neither required to recognize nor prohibited from recognizing UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters in format 1 alphanumeric literals. When permitted, the capability shall be optionally available to the user in a manner that does not restrict the characters normally recognized by that implementation; the implementor shall specify any applicable syntax rules.

rows.subject: Alphanumeric literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "shall be in the same coded character set representation as the opening quotation symbol" OK. The lexer recognizes exactly two delimiter code points (U+0022, U+0027) and the doubled pair is written as the same code point as the opener in STR_BODY, so a pair in a different representation (e.g. U+FF02 FULLWIDTH QUOTATION MARK) is never taken as a doubled delimiter -- it is ordinary content. Satisfied by construction; no spec-derived test isolates it. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held)
rows.rule-text: The two contiguous quotation symbols used to represent a single quotation symbol character shall be in the same coded character set representation as the opening quotation symbol.
